notes:
Opportunity: ThreadMinder builds an orchestration layer for mid-size contact centers (retail & telco verticals). They are extremely cost-sensitive: target unit economics = <$0.03 per deflected conversation, aiming for 50-70% deflection on FAQ-heavy flows.

POC scope: 2-week POC using 200K historical chats + live shadow traffic to validate batching/caching and quantization impact on latency/quality. Focus areas: continuous batching heuristics, KV/prefix caching for session context, 4-bit quantized model variants for cheap bulk inference, and per-route routing policies to fallback to smaller models during spikes.

Performance targets (stated):
- Peak concurrency: 6k concurrent short chat sessions during promo spikes
- Throughput target: ~30k messages/day for initial rollout, scale to 150k/day in 6 months
- Latency SLO: P50 < 250ms token latency for hosted/dedicated; P95 budgeted at <1.2s for short responses

Security & compliance: customer requires SOC2 plus audit logs mapped to ticket IDs, SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, and EU data residency for EU customers. On-prem not required currently but legal wants clause for future on_prem option.

Cost sensitivity notes: CFO expects detailed unit economics before procurement. They asked for per-route cost estimates, batching sensitivity analysis, cache hit-rate modeling, and quantization tradeoff doc. Quote must show committed reserved capacity vs burst pricing.

Quotes from stakeholders: "We need predictable bills when Black Friday hits — last year we paid 3x for baseline traffic spikes." — Head of Ops.

Technical risks / ES cales: current agent UI integrates via websocket API, needs <300ms roundtrip for ideal UX. Concern about KV cache staleness and multi-tenant memory growth. SE recommended a prototype with cache sharding + TTL policies.

Links: shared sample prompt deck (drive link above), transcript ff_2026-01-12 contains product manager comments on fallback policies.
